messages.content: Kal mujhe interview hai, how to introduce myself? Mera naam Rohit hai aur maine B.Com kiya hai.

Here is a simple introduction you can use: "Good morning. My name is Rohit. I have completed my B.Com, and I am keen to start my career in this field." Keep it short, speak slowly and look at the interviewer when you talk.
Please correct my sentence: Yesterday I go to school and teacher give us many homework.

Corrected: "Yesterday I went to school, and the teacher gave us a lot of homework." Use the past tense (went, gave) with "yesterday". Say "the teacher". "Homework" cannot be counted, so say "a lot of homework", not "many homework".
Mummy ko kaise bolun in English ki main late aaungi aaj? I want to send her a message.
You can write: "Mummy, I will be late today. I will be home by eight." Change the time to match your plans.
Aur agar main bolna chahun ki don't worry, I'm with friends?
Add this line: "Don't worry, I am with my friends." The full message becomes: "Mummy, I will be late today. Don't worry, I am with my friends. I will be home by eight."
What is meaning of 'tiffin' in proper English? My friend from UK not understanding.

In India, "tiffin" means a packed lunch or a light meal. Most people in Britain today say "packed lunch" or "lunch box". You could tell your friend, "Tiffin is the lunch I bring from home." Also, a small fix for your question: "What is the meaning of 'tiffin'? My friend from the UK does not understand."
Auto wale bhaiya ko English mein kaise bolun ki station jaana hai?
You can say: "Please take me to the railway station." If you want to ask the fare first, say: "How much to the railway station?"
Agar woh zyada paise maange toh?
You can say politely: "That is too much. Can you do it for less?" Or: "Please use the meter." Keep your voice calm and friendly.
And how to say 'yahin rok dijiye'?
Say: "Please stop here." You can also say, "You can drop me here, thank you."
I am writing mail to my boss: 'Sir, I am having fever since two days so I am not able to come.' Is it correct?

Almost. A better version: "Sir, I have had a fever for two days, so I will not be able to come to the office today." Use "have had" for something that started in the past and is still true. Use "for" with a length of time, like "two days".
Holi ke baare mein 3 lines likhni hain English mein, school project ke liye.

Here are three simple lines:
1. Holi is the festival of colours, celebrated in spring.
2. People play with coloured powder and water, and share sweets like gujiya.
3. Holi brings friends and families together in joy.
Thanks! Gujiya ko English mein kya bolte hain?
There is no exact English word for it. You can keep "gujiya" and explain it once: "a sweet dumpling filled with khoya and dry fruits". Many Indian food names stay the same in English.
Which is right: 'He is my best friend since childhood' or 'He has been my best friend since childhood'?
The second one is right: "He has been my best friend since childhood." When something started in the past and is still true now, use the present perfect (has been) with "since".
Aaj mera mood bahut off hai. English mein kaise bolun ki main sad feel kar raha hoon but reason nahi pata?
You can say: "I'm feeling low today, and I don't know why." Another way is: "I'm feeling a bit down for no clear reason."
Theek hai. Aur dost ko kaise bolun ki mujhe thoda time chahiye akele?
You can say: "I need a little time to myself today. It's not about you." The second sentence helps your friend understand that you're not upset with them. I hope the low feeling passes soon.
In shop I say 'Give me one kg potato.' My cousin says it sounds rude. How to say better?
Your cousin has a point. Add "please" and use the plural: "Could I have one kilo of potatoes, please?" Or simply: "One kilo of potatoes, please." Both sound polite and natural.
Teacher ne bola procrastinate mat karo. Iska matlab kya hai?

"Procrastinate" means to keep delaying something you should do, often by doing easier things instead. It is a verb. Example: "I procrastinated all evening and started my homework at ten." Your teacher meant: do your work now, and don't keep putting it off.
When I pick phone in office I say 'Yes, tell.' My manager said change it. What I should say?

A more polite opening is: "Hello, this is Neha from Accounts. How can I help you?" Use your own name and team instead. It tells the caller who they have reached. Also, a small fix: "What should I say?"
And if I don't understand what they said?
Say: "Sorry, could you repeat that, please?" or "Sorry, I didn't catch that." Both are polite and very common.
My manager also said don't say 'do the needful'. Why?
"Do the needful" is understood in India, but many English speakers find it old-fashioned or unclear. It's better to say exactly what you need, for example: "Please send me the report by Friday."
Recipe English mein likhni hai. 'Pyaaz ko golden hone tak bhuno' ka translation?
In English: "Fry the onions until they turn golden brown." In recipes you will also see the shorter "Fry the onions until golden." Both are correct.
I am going abroad first time. At immigration, what questions they ask usually?

First, a small fix: "I am going abroad for the first time. What questions do they usually ask?" Common ones are: "What is the purpose of your visit?", "How long will you stay?" and "Where will you stay?" Give short, clear answers.
How I answer the first one? I am going for my sister wedding.
Say: "I'm here for my sister's wedding." Note the apostrophe and s in "sister's". It shows that the wedding is your sister's.
Match haarne ke baad coach ko English mein kya bolun? Kuch acha sa.
You could say: "Thank you for training us, Coach. We lost today, but we learned a lot, and we'll work harder for the next match." It's honest, and it shows you respect the coach's effort.
My neighbour aunty invited me for dinner. How to say no politely? I have exam.
You can say: "Thank you so much for inviting me, Aunty. I'd love to come, but I have an exam tomorrow. Could I visit another day?" Offering another day keeps it warm.
Is 'I'd love to' too much? We are not very close.
It isn't too much. "I'd love to come, but..." is a normal, polite way to say no in English. If you want something simpler, say: "Thank you, Aunty, but I can't come tonight because of my exam."
Dukaan wale ko kaise bolun ki mere paas change nahi hai, sirf 500 ka note hai?
You can say: "Sorry, I don't have change. I only have a 500-rupee note." If you need him to break it, ask: "Do you have change for 500?"
Is it 'It is raining heavily' or 'It is raining heavy'?
Say "It is raining heavily." You need the adverb "heavily" because it describes the verb "raining". You can also say, "There is heavy rain," where the adjective "heavy" describes the noun "rain".
Mujhe English newspaper padhna hai but bahut words samajh nahi aate. Kya karun?

Start small. Read one short news story each day, not the whole paper. Underline three new words, look them up, and write one sentence with each. After a few weeks, you will notice the same words coming back.
Aur speaking ke liye?
Read that same story aloud once. Then tell it to someone in your own words, in two or three sentences. It feels slow at first, but it builds speaking and reading together.
I want wish my friend for birthday in english but not boring. Please help.

First, a small fix: "I want to wish my friend a happy birthday." Here is a fun message: "Happy birthday! Another year older, but still the person who laughs loudest in class. Have a wonderful day!" Change the middle line to something true about your friend.
